content: The Cranfield evaluation paradigm provides the foundational methodology for benchmark evaluation in information retrieval. Set-based retrieval metrics include Recall@K, Precision@K, and HitRate@K. For a fixed evaluation cutoff K, Recall@K measures the proportion of all relevant documents successfully retrieved in the top-K candidate list. HitRate@K is a binary metric indicating whether at least one relevant document appears within the top-K results. In standard evaluation sweeps, cutoffs K=5 and K=10 are established as the primary operating points for sparse and dense retrieval systems.

Positional metrics evaluate ranking quality by penalizing relevant documents that appear further down the ranked list. Mean Reciprocal Rank (MRR@K) computes the mean of the reciprocal rank 1/rank_i, where rank_i is the one-based rank position of the first relevant document returned for query i. If no relevant document appears within the top-K positions, the reciprocal rank for that query is assigned 0.0. MRR is especially suited for known-item search and question answering systems where the user seeks a single decisive answer.

Normalized Discounted Cumulative Gain (NDCG@K) evaluates retrieval systems supporting multi-level graded relevance. Discounted Cumulative Gain is calculated as DCG@K = sum_{i=1}^K (2^{r_i} - 1) / log2(i + 1), where r_i represents the relevance grade of the document at rank position i. The ideal DCG (IDCG@K) is the DCG score achieved by an optimal sorting of all relevant items. The normalized score NDCG@K = DCG@K / IDCG@K ranges from 0.0 to 1.0. When a query has no relevant items in the corpus, NDCG is defined as 0.0.

AI Reliability Lab establishes a strict 3-tier graded relevance scale for benchmark construction: Grade 0 (Irrelevant) indicates a chunk containing non-pertinent information or a misleading lexical distractor; Grade 1 (Relevant Context) indicates a chunk that provides supportive, topical context but lacks the complete evidence required to formulate an authoritative answer; Grade 2 (Critical Evidence) indicates a chunk that directly states the decisive factual claim needed to answer the query.

Lexical versus semantic retrieval exhibits distinct trade-offs across Cranfield benchmarks. While dense vector embedding models capture semantic paraphrasing and conceptual similarity, exact lexical matching engines like BM25 are indispensable for specific entity names, product model codes, alphanumeric IDs, and rare vocabulary. In hybrid retrieval architectures, combining lexical and dense retrievers prevents vocabulary mismatch regressions while preserving precision on technical entity lookups.

The PyMuPDF document parser extracts textual and geometric provenance from PDF documents. All character offsets into Document.content are represented as zero-based, half-open intervals [char_start, char_end). For every extracted page, line, and text span, the parser enforces the exact invariant that slicing Document.content[char_start:char_end] reproduces the recorded text string without character drift or normalization loss.

Document parsing enforces deterministic separators during text assembly: consecutive lines within a page are separated by a single newline '
', while consecutive pages are separated by a double newline '

'. Global character offsets are computed against the fully assembled buffer including separators, ensuring that page boundary transitions never shift subsequent character coordinates.

SlidingWindowChunker divides source documents into fixed-size overlapping character windows. Given a configured chunk_size and chunk_overlap, the window step size is calculated as step = chunk_size - chunk_overlap. Because chunk_overlap is strictly constrained to be less than chunk_size, the step size is guaranteed to be at least 1, preventing infinite loops during chunk generation.

RecursiveCharacterChunker applies an ordered priority of semantic separators: double newlines '

' for paragraphs, single newlines '
' for lines, periods with trailing space '. ' for sentences, spaces ' ' for words, and the empty string '' as character-level fallback. Separators remain attached to the preceding text slice, ensuring that all resulting atomic pieces partition Document.content without dropping characters.

Page provenance attribution in chunking requires strict zero-leakage boundaries. If a chunk falls strictly within a single source page, Chunk.page_number is assigned that one-based page integer. If a chunk spans across multiple pages or across unmapped page boundary separators, Chunk.page_number is set to None, and the complete list of intersecting page records is retained in Chunk.metadata['pages'].

Okapi BM25 is an established probabilistic sparse retrieval algorithm. The parameter k1 controls term frequency saturation, governing how rapidly additional occurrences of a term approach the upper asymptote; the default is k1 = 1.5. The parameter b controls document length normalization, penalizing longer documents relative to the corpus average document length avgdl; the default is b = 0.75.

The Robertson-Spärck Jones formula for inverse document frequency is defined as IDF(t) = ln(1 + (N - df(t) + 0.5) / (df(t) + 0.5)), where N is the total number of indexed chunks and df(t) is the document frequency of term t. The addition of 1.0 inside the logarithm ensures that IDF values remain strictly non-negative for all terms, avoiding negative score contributions even when a term appears in more than half the corpus.

Dense semantic retrieval generates dense vector embeddings using the sentence-transformers model 'all-MiniLM-L6-v2'. This model maps input chunk text into a 384-dimensional dense vector space. All generated vector embeddings are L2-normalized so that inner product calculations directly correspond to cosine similarities, allowing efficient nearest-neighbor search without dynamic vector magnitude scaling.

FAISS vector indexing provides both exact and approximate search modalities. IndexFlatIP performs exhaustive inner product comparison with 100% recall guarantee at the expense of linear O(N) search time. In contrast, IndexHNSWFlat constructs a hierarchical navigable small-world graph, providing approximate nearest neighbor retrieval with logarithmic O(log N) search latency suitable for production workloads.

Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) combines ranked lists from sparse (BM25) and dense (FAISS) retrievers without requiring score normalization. The fusion score for document d across retrievers M is given by RRF(d) = sum_{m in M} 1 / (k + r_m(d)), where r_m(d) is the rank of document d in retriever m and k is a ranking constant typically set to k = 60. RRF prevents score scale discrepancies between algorithms from skewing the final ranking.

Groundedness auditing evaluates whether every factual statement generated by an AI model is explicitly substantiated by retrieved source documents. An ungrounded claim occurs when an assertion cannot be mapped to any citation in the evidence context. In automated audits, citation verification engines verify that each factual claim is paired with a corresponding source chunk ID and verbatim character quote.

Citation evaluation measures two complementary dimensions: citation precision and citation recall. Citation precision is the ratio of supporting citations to total citations provided: Precision_cit = N_valid_citations / N_total_citations. Citation recall is the ratio of substantiated factual claims to total verifiable claims: Recall_cit = N_substantiated_claims / N_total_claims. High citation precision ensures no misleading references, while high citation recall ensures no unsupported assertions.

Hallucinations in document-based question answering are classified into intrinsic and extrinsic types. An intrinsic hallucination contradicts or distorts facts explicitly present in the source context, such as misstating a numerical quantity or reversing a causal direction. An extrinsic hallucination introduces external facts or fabricated entities that are completely unmentioned in the source documents, regardless of whether they happen to be true in the real world.

Automated quality guardrails enforce strict citation thresholds for high-stakes enterprise deployments. The pipeline triggers an automated rejection alert if citation precision falls below 95% or if any ungrounded factual assertion is identified in the response. Responses failing this threshold are blocked from presentation and routed to human audit queues.

Human verification protocol requires dual-annotator agreement before golden benchmark queries and relevance judgments are approved. Annotators independently verify that ground-truth answers are strictly derivable from cited evidence. The inter-annotator agreement threshold requires Cohen's kappa kappa >= 0.85 across relevance grades, ensuring high consistency and eliminating subjective annotator bias.

Performance and latency budgets for in-memory lexical retrieval require tight runtime guarantees. In AI Reliability Lab, the in-memory Okapi BM25 engine is architected to achieve a p99 latency target of 25ms for search queries across corpora of up to 100,000 chunks. Query latency is monitored using high-resolution monotonic timers to detect performance regressions during continuous integration.

High-concurrency query processing utilizes read-only inverted index snapshots protected by reader-writer locks. Concurrent evaluation runs can execute multiple simultaneous benchmark query sweeps without read-lock contention, enabling parallel evaluation of sparse BM25, dense FAISS, and hybrid fusion pipelines across multiple worker threads.

Memory footprint guidelines dictate efficient data structures for in-memory inverted indices. By packing document postings into contiguous integer lists and storing unique terms in shared interned string tables, the in-memory BM25 index consumes less than 15MB RAM per 10,000 indexed text chunks, allowing large evaluation suites to run entirely within developer workstation memory without external database services.

Automated regression detection gates continuous deployment by benchmarking evaluation metrics on every git pull request. An automated regression failure is triggered if Mean Reciprocal Rank (MRR@5) degrades by more than 2.0% or if p99 query latency increases by more than 15% compared to the verified baseline recorded on the main branch.

Reproducible benchmark execution environments require strict hardware isolation during regression measurement runs. The evaluation runner disables CPU dynamic frequency scaling, pins worker processes to dedicated physical CPU cores, and runs warm-up iterations to eliminate cold-start cache anomalies before recording official benchmark timings.
